claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I need to gather some information about your situation.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex. Now I need to understand your living situation to determine eligibility.

**Do you live with Alex in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK, but Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, there are still potential ways you could qualify for Child Benefit. Let me ask you about this:

**Are you currently making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money, or help with accommodation costs)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out. I contribute towards his clothes and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. To properly assess your eligibility, I need to understand the level and consistency of your contributions:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's upkeep each week or month, and how regularly do you make these payments?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £10 a week towards his upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. Now I need to check one more important thing about the current situation:

**Is Alex's mum currently receiving Child Benefit for Alex, or do you know whether anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, his mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me explain the situation: According to the Child Benefit rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex's mum is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be eligible to claim it as well.

The rules do state that you could potentially continue to receive Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else if nobody else is claiming. However, since someone else (Alex's mum) is already claiming, this doesn't apply to your situation.

Additionally, while you are making contributions towards Alex's upkeep, those contributions would only help you continue to claim if you were already receiving Child Benefit before he moved to live with his mum - they wouldn't allow you to start a new claim when someone else is already claiming for that child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'm sorry that you're not eligible to claim Child Benefit in this case. However, it's good that you're helping to support Alex with regular contributions towards his upkeep. If circumstances change in the future - for example, if his mother stops claiming Child Benefit - you may be able to claim at that point. You could contact HMRC's Child Benefit Office if you have any further questions or if your situation changes.
